fixes: Natural style: reads as a shard-edged boat/bowl, not a rock-lined stream (canonical.jpg). Concept (04-arrival-gate) has rounded, mossless boulders with flat tops that overlap and shelter the water, a clear channel bed with cobbles, and low weirs. Replace the spiky wedge rocks with lumpy rounded boulders (0.25-0.5 m, bevel radius ~4-6 cm) and flatten the banks to a 0.2-0.35 m high lip. Add a visible stone bed and 2-3 weir lips (0.1-0.17 m drop).

Kerbed style: the kerb is a single plain beam with a flat water ramp; no coursing. Sheet-vs-water-2 #2 shows coursed ashlar sides (~0.15 m course height, staggered) with a capstone and 0.17 m steps. Break the kerb into 0.4-0.8 m blocks with 3-5 mm joint bevels, add a 2 cm capstone overhang, and make the bed horizontal pools separated by 0.17 m weirs rather than one sloped plane.

Stepped style: reads as stacked cuboids with the weir treads unclear. Concept stepped runnel is a stair of ashlar with a 0.17 m drop per step and water sheeting over each lip. Make each step a full-width tread (tread depth 0.3-0.4 m) with a rounded lip, and put side walls at the same coursing. Currently the kerb blocks rise higher than the steps and hide the flow.

Scale: kerbed and stepped widths (0.4-0.8 m) with 0.14 m kerbs look chunky; the natural bank reaches ~0.6 m high shards. Hold the sheet scale: width 0.3-0.5 m inner, kerb 0.12 m, wall height 0.25-0.35 m above bed for the rill.

LOD2/LOD3: at 35-131 m the form is a speck and LOD3 seed 2 is a 10-tri strip. Acceptable range but keep the bed colour/emissive tag so the water ribbon reads; and fix the LOD pop where natural LOD2 flips from rocks to a smooth sheet (silhouette becomes a plain curved plane).
Missing lantern/cobble dressing is not required, but add optional cobble scatter in the bed (8-12 stones, 4-8 cm) at LOD0/1 so the shallow water reads as shallow.
library_issues: basalt_wet bank rocks read as brown-grey matte metal with white spec streaks, not wet black basalt
paving on kerbs reads flat tan-grey with no joint pattern; needs a visible block/joint texture
water_river bed is a flat teal sheet (fx will replace); fine
summary: Three styles differ clearly (good variation) but none matches the concept: natural is a spiky bowl, kerbed a plain trough with ramp water, stepped a stack of boxes. Needs rounded boulder banks, coursed ashlar kerbs and true 0.17 m weirs.
